title: A barque at the outer bar
body:
Late August 1511. Most of the Cambay houses have shut their doors; the ships that escaped July's fires have already made for Pasai and Pedir. The Cambay Shahbandar's circle has vanished from the lanes.

At dusk a boatman brings word from Khoja Ismail's factor. Because you held the Salamat quietly and kept Farid's name off the quay, Ismail has kept a chartered barque waiting off the outer bar. His factor offers passage north for your clerk and office chests, or a witnessed copy of the Salamat's shore receipts before he slips away on the tide.

choices.label: Send your clerk and chests aboard Ismail's barque
choices.outcome_text: The chests go out in the dark with the last resin lots. By morning the outer bar is empty, and your accounts are bound for Pasai.

choices.label: Stay ashore and take his witnessed receipts for the closing roll
choices.outcome_text: Ismail's factor signs the shore tally by lantern light before casting off. Even after the sack, one house's account closes clean.

notes: fact: Gujarati shipping suffered fire during the July 1511 blockade and much western Muslim trade shifted toward Pasai and Aceh after the fall, though Pires later notes some Gujaratis returning (docs/research/1511-events.md §1, Phases III & V; docs/research/people-factions.md §3).

gameplay: Khoja Ismail, Farid, the Salamat and the chartered barque are fictional continuations of data/merchants/khoja_ismail.json and data/inspections/case_004.json. The Cambay Shahbandar remains unnamed per docs/research/people-factions.md §2.
